Therefore, the increase in predicted traffic generated noise level between a "Do-Nothing" and "To Improve the Facility" would yield a similar noise level regardless of whether or not the improvement is implemented.
C. To Improve This Highway Facility
Lincoln Highway presently passes through a heavily urbanized area where residential and business property has been built-up close to the existing right-of-way limits. Moving the proposed improvement to the north of the present location of Lincoln Highway would require extensive land taking through the heart of a substantial residential area in the City of Chicago Heights at prohibitive cost. The northern location would have required a large land taking from the Cook County Forest Preserve at the eastern terminus of the improvement. It would have also required a complete relocation of the Illinois Central Railroad Commuter station in the Village of Olympia Fields, and would have required land taking from the Village parklands west of Olympian Way.
Moving the proposed improvement to the south of the present location of Lincoln Highway would pose much the same problem as moving it to the north. Extensive residential land takings would be required. Also, large portions of two City of Chicago Heights parks would be taken for highway purposes. In the Village of Matteson, two cemeteries would also be extensively damaged.
Relocating the improvement either north or south of the present Lincoln Highway location would pose severe problems. Extensive right-of-way takings would be required. Furthermore, Lincoln Highway presently acts as a natural neighborhood and school attendance boundary and any major change in its location would be disruptive to established community life.
Interstate Route 80 has been constructed to the north of Lincoln Highway and there is a proposed east-west freeway under study in a corridor several miles to the south. The eastern terminus of the proposed improvement is controlled by a newly completed improvement from Chicago Road eastward through the City of Chicago Heights.
